channel.description: Debezium is an open source distributed platform for change data capture. Start it up, point it at your databases, and your apps can start responding to all of the inserts, updates, and deletes that other apps commit to your databases. Debezium is durable and fast, so your apps can respond quickly and never miss an event, even when things go wrong.

item.title: Single Sign-On for the Debezium Platform
item.dc:creator: Philippe Camus
item.description:
Identity and Access Management is a highly anticipated feature for the Debezium Platform, slatted for Q4.

Until then, we can explore what is currently possible: Single Sign-on, OpenID Connect, and even brokering Entra ID. In this first post, I will walk you through putting a Debezium Platform deployment on Kubernetes behind a single sign-on (SSO) login with Keycloak as an Identity Provider.

The scenario throughout the blog series is Contoso Retail, a fictional company on the domain contoso.com, running the Platform on a Kubernetes cluster and wanting its own staff list to govern access to it. Contoso Retail uses Entra ID as its corporate directory.

item.title: Debezium 3.7.0.Beta1 Released
item.dc:creator: Chris Cranford
item.description:
As summer continues, we’re excited to announce the release of Debezium 3.7.0.Beta1, bringing a broad set of improvements across connectors, Debezium Server, and the Platform UI.

Among the highlights, incremental snapshots now work on PostgreSQL read-only replicas, and Debezium Server gains a new Databricks ZeroBus Ingest sink for direct change event delivery to Unity Catalog-managed Delta tables. This release also includes performance and snapshot optimizations, new connector capabilities, and numerous bug fixes across the board.

Read on for the full details!

item.title: Debezium 3.7.0.Alpha2 Released
item.dc:creator: Chris Cranford
item.description:
We’re pleased to announce the release of Debezium 3.7.0.Alpha2, the second preview release in the 3.7 series, packed with new features and important changes across the platform.

This release introduces an incubating TiDB connector, adds retry and dead letter queue support for the JDBC sink, and improves Debezium Server with a proper readiness probe. On the Oracle side, the OpenLogReplicator client is now non-blocking and continuous mining for Oracle 12 has been removed. The Debezium Platform UI now surfaces pipeline failures directly, and several other connectors receive important fixes and improvements.

Let’s take a closer look at all these changes and more; read on for the full details!

item.title: Debezium 3.6.1.Final Released
item.dc:creator: Chris Cranford
item.description:
We’re pleased to announce the release of Debezium 3.6.1.Final, a maintenance release that delivers important data integrity and security improvements across multiple connectors.

This release fixes several issues that could affect change event accuracy, including correct parsing of BC-era dates in PostgreSQL, proper mapping of MySQL INTEGER UNSIGNED columns, and resolution of Oracle RowId corruption in change events. The JDBC sink connector also receives a fix for tsvector data handling, and credential leakage has been addressed in log output and configuration serialization.

Read on for the full details!

item.title: Running the Debezium Platform on AWS: PostgreSQL to Amazon Kinesis
item.dc:creator: Philippe Camus
item.description:
In his recent mid-year update, Mario highlighted the incredible work he and his team have done to make the Debezium Platform operational on Kubernetes. So let us take it somewhere concrete: Amazon Web Services.

This post stands the Platform up on a single-node k3s cluster on an EC2 instance and builds a real change-data-capture pipeline from Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL to Amazon Kinesis. The deployment itself is done through a couple of simple commands via a companion project that does the heavy lifting, so the focus is the AWS-specific friction that documentation is thin on: IAM for the Kinesis sink, Kinesis stream naming, RDS logical replication, and reading a change event back out of the stream to prove it all works.

item.title: No More Tuning: Oracle Log Mining Simplified in Debezium 3.6
item.dc:creator: Chris Cranford
item.description:
If you have ever deployed the Debezium Oracle connector in an environment with bursty workloads, you have probably spent more time than you would like tuning the log.mining.batch.size.*, log.mining.sleep.time.*, and log.mining.scn.gap.detection.* properties. Getting the balance right between peak and quiet periods was, frankly, a losing battle — what worked for your nightly ETL window would over-read during the day, and what worked during the day would fall hopelessly behind at night.

In Debezium 3.6, we replaced this entire mechanism. The connector now selects mining windows based on log file count rather than SCN ranges, controlled by a single new property: log.mining.log.count.min. This post explains why the old approach was so hard to tune, how the new approach works, and what you need to know to migrate.


Read more...

item.title: Building Kafka-Less Data Integration Pipelines with Debezium
item.dc:creator: Fiore Mario Vitale
item.description:
Debezium is often associated with Kafka, and while this was true in the project’s early days, it is no longer the case. We explained in detail, together with several other common misconceptions, in our recent article, "What Nobody Explains About Debezium in 2026 (But Should)".

In this article, we’ll build on that discussion by showing the recently added JDBC sink support in Debezium Server (DS) and the Debezium Management Platform (DMP), which opens up Kafka-less data replication and migration scenarios.

item.title: Debezium Community Showcase
item.dc:creator: Giovanni Panice
item.description:
It has been a month since we opened our weekly team meeting to the community, and we have received many interesting insights. Because of that, we have decided to create another opportunity for the community to connect and share:

Welcome to the Debezium Community Showcase!

Starting next month, we will host a monthly showcase session that will be live-streamed on YouTube. Whether you would like to share something about CDC with Debezium, how you use Debezium in your work, or anything related to contributing to the project, you are welcome to submit a talk.

However, if there is not enough content for a given month, the showcase may be postponed to the following month.

Session Proposal and Participation

To keep track of talks, session proposals will be managed through Sessionize.

Community members are encouraged to first propose a session in our weekly forum for a brief evaluation, and then formally submit the proposal through Sessionize so that we can schedule it on the calendar.

Format of Sessions

We have two kind of sessions based on duration:

  • Lightning Talks: 10-15min duration

  • Standard talks: 30 duration

Calendar and Scheduling

The showcase will be scheduled on a Tuesday and will take place during the weekly forum, depending on the Debezium team’s schedule and the available content. The showcase will last up to 1 hour and may include one lightning talk and one standard talk, with a few additional minutes for questions.

We truly believe these sessions provide another great opportunity to share, discuss, and exchange ideas that help shape the future of Debezium.

We look forward to seeing your insights!

item.title: Debezium 3.6.0.CR1 Released
item.dc:creator: Chris Cranford
item.description:
As we approach the final stages of the Debezium 3.6 release cycle, we’re excited to announce the release of Debezium 3.6.0.CR1, the first candidate release for this milestone.

This release delivers several notable enhancements, including Spanner Omni compatibility, a monitoring REST API and multi-panel dashboard in Debezium Platform, JDBC sink support in Platform, off-heap memory management for table history and schemas using RocksDB, and performance improvements that significantly reduce allocation and CPU overhead in the MySQL connector’s poll path. On the bug-fix front, this release resolves a KafkaSchemaHistory recovery race condition, PostgreSQL varbit column handling, Vitess timestamp processing, NanoTimestamp overflow for extreme dates, and CockroachDB temporal type alignment.

Read on for all the details!

item.dc:creator: Chris Cranford
item.description:
As the Debezium 3.6 development cycle continues, we’re pleased to announce Debezium 3.6.0.Beta2, a feature-rich release with significant improvements across the platform.

This release introduces MySQL GTID tags support, a new Debezium CLI, and Spanner UUID support. The Quarkus Extensions gain column change filtering for both single and batch event capturing, a start and stop lifecycle API, and multi-engine improvements. MySQL and MariaDB connectors now offer customizable zero-date fallback values, the Platform Helm Chart adds OpenTelemetry Collector deployment, and Apicurio has been upgraded to version 3.2.5.

item.title: Debezium 3.6.0.Beta1 Released
item.dc:creator: Chris Cranford
item.description:
We’re excited to announce the release of Debezium 3.6.0.Beta1, which brings a wealth of new features and improvements to the Debezium ecosystem.

This release upgrades to Apache Kafka 4.3, introduces an incubating Apache Fluss sink adapter for Debezium Server, adds an incubating YashanDB source connector, and deprecates the redo_log_catalog Oracle mining strategy. On the operations side, the Debezium Operator now supports OpenTelemetry configuration and configurable image pull policies. Additional highlights include PostgreSQL publication-level skipped operations propagation, a new message-size-aware column truncation feature for Vitess, and a compatibility fix for MongoDB 8.0+ containers on recent Linux kernels.

item.title: What Nobody Explains About Debezium in 2026 (But Should)
item.dc:creator: Chris Cranford
item.description:
Teams evaluating Change Data Capture (CDC) tools often encounter comparison articles with titles like "Top Debezium Alternatives in 2026" or "Why We Moved Away from Debezium." These articles can be useful starting points for evaluation, but many rely on characterizations that reflect older deployment patterns rather than Debezium’s current capabilities.

Debezium is not the right fit for every team or every use case, and we will be upfront about that in this post. Different CDC tools optimize for different goals: some prioritize turnkey SaaS experiences, others focus on tightly integrated transformation pipelines, and Debezium optimizes for openness, composability, database breadth, and deployment flexibility. Understanding these tradeoffs is more useful than debating which tool is "best."

This post addresses common questions that arise during CDC evaluations, with an honest look at where Debezium fits and where other approaches might serve your team better.

item.title: Debezium welcomes its Google Summer of Code 2026 Contributors!
item.dc:creator: Giovanni Panice
item.description:
We’re excited to share the next milestone in Debezium’s Google Summer of Code 2026 journey: our contributors have been selected, and the community bonding period has officially started! 🎉

Earlier this year, we announced that Debezium would participate in Google Summer of Code 2026 as part of the JBoss Community organization, offering project ideas focused on change data capture, vector databases, Quarkus, AI/ML, developer tooling, and the Debezium platform. Since then, we’ve had many interesting conversations with prospective contributors, reviewed proposals, and worked together to select the projects that will move forward this year.

The official GSoC 2026 timeline announced accepted contributors on April 30th, followed by the community bonding period from May 1st to May 24th. Coding will officially begin on May 25th.

Meet Our GSoC 2026 Contributors

We’re happy to welcome the contributors to the Debezium community for the following projects:

Debezium CLI

summary: Debezium CLI would provide developers and operators with a streamlined way to create, manage, and monitor CDC pipelines across data systems.

Contributor: Binayak Das

Proposal: link

About the contributor: Binayak Das is a Computer Science and Engineering student from India very interested in Java backend systems, AI/ML, developer tooling and open source software. He has contributed to organisations such as Scala3, OpenMRS and Debezium since in his first year of college.

Mentors: Giovanni Panice, Mario Fiore Vitale

Host-Based Pipeline Deployment for the Debezium Platform

summary: The project idea is to provide support for running Debezium on bare metal, virtual machines, and cloud services, using Debezium Server distributions (container images and standalone packages).

Contributor: Divyanshu Kumar

Proposal: link

About the contributor: Divyanshu Kumar is a CSE student and Software Engineer from India focused on high-performance backends and cloud-native systems. A two-time GSoC contributor, C4GT, and SOB participant, he has experience with Java, GWT, and event-driven platforms

Mentors: Mario Fiore Vitale, Giovanni Panice

PyDebeziumAI

summary: The project aims to build an intelligent, Python‑native framework for real‑time reasoning over Change Data Capture (CDC) streams by integrating the capabilities of pydbzengine with modern AI/LLM‑powered Python libraries.

Contributor: Kodukulla Mohnish Mythreya

Proposal: link

About the contributor: Kodukulla Mohnish Mythreya is a 3rd-year CSE student at VIT Chennai and Development Lead at CYSCOM, interested in AI, cloud, developer tooling, and real-time data systems. As a GSoC 2026 contributor with JBoss Community, he’ll work on PyDebeziumAI for real-time CDC reasoning.

Mentors: Jiri Pechanec, Vojtěch Juránek

Debezium Source Connector for Milvus

summary: The project aims to build a Source Connector for Milvus, a vector database designed to power modern AI/ML applications, including semantic search, recommendation systems, RAG (Retrieval‑Augmented Generation), and multimodal search.

Contributor: Kartik Angiras

Proposal: link

About the contributor: Kartik is a tech agnostic developer with an experience in Backend construction, Blockchain engineering and System Design. His open source experience ranges from CDC platforms such as Debezium, Cloud Native projects such as Kyverno, Prometheus Operator, Antrea along with Gemini CLI, Swift etc.

Mentors: Chris Cranford, Giovanni Panice

Debezium Source Connector for Sqlite

summary: The project aims to build a Source Connector for Sqlite, an embedded relational database engine built around a simple architecture where the entire database, including schema, data, and indexes resides in a single cross‑platform file

Contributor: Siddhant Chaturvedi

Proposal: link

About the contributor: Siddhant is a student at IIIT Gwalior with a strong foundation in full-stack development and a passion for system design. He loves exploring backend architecture and large-scale data systems. Away from the keyboard, you will find him swapping his IDE for a camera or a digital canvas.

Mentors: Vincenzo Santonastaso, Giovanni Panice

A Big Thank You to All Applicants

We received many thoughtful proposals and had great discussions with prospective contributors. We want to thank everyone who took the time to learn about Debezium, join the community channels, ask questions, prepare an application and a special thanks to all who submitted any patch as part of getting familiar with Debezium.

If your proposal was not selected this year, we still encourage you to stay involved. GSoC is only one way to contribute to Debezium. The project is open all year round, and we’re always happy to welcome new contributors through issues, documentation improvements, bug fixes, discussions, and feature proposals.

What’s next

We’re looking forward to a productive and exciting summer of open-source collaboration. The selected projects will help expand the Debezium ecosystem and improve the experience for developers working with change data capture. As coding begins, we’ll share updates about the progress of each project and highlight the work our contributors are doing.

Welcome to GSoC 2026 contributors for Debezium, we’re excited to have you with us! 🚀

This release brings Informix JDBC driver v15 support, resolves a Debezium Server startup failure, fixes incorrect bytecode generation in the CockroachDB connector, and improves handling of PostgreSQL infinity timestamps in nanosecond precision mode. item.title: Join the Debezium Community Weekly Forum
item.dc:creator: Indra Raj Shukla
item.description:
The Debezium community grows through open collaboration among users, contributors, maintainers, and the wider data-streaming ecosystem.

Starting Tuesday, May 19, we are opening our weekly team meeting on every Tuesday to the broader Debezium community. Whether you are a contributor, evaluating Debezium, or simply interested in change data capture and streaming, you are welcome to attend.

The meeting duration is scheduled for 45 minutes. However, to respect everyone’s time, meetings may conclude earlier if the agenda is completed and there are no extra topic for discussion. The minimum meeting duration will be 15 minutes.

Meeting Agenda and Participation

To keep the meetings transparent and collaborative, the agenda is maintained in a shared Google Document that is open for external comments and suggestions.

You can view the agenda document here:

Debezium Community Meeting Agenda

Community members are encouraged to propose topics, discussion items, demos, questions, or updates ahead of the meeting.

New discussion topics should first be proposed on Zulip, so the maintainers can help shape the discussion and decide whether it should be added to an upcoming meeting agenda.

Request to add a topic to the agenda via Zulip:

Debezium Forum Agenda

Calendar and Scheduling

Debezium community meetings and events are listed in our shared Google Calendar. You can browse the schedule online or subscribe to the public iCalendar feed to keep upcoming events in your own calendar application.

Public calendar:

Debezium Community Calendar

We hope these meetings provide another accessible way for the community to collaborate, exchange ideas, discuss roadmap items, highlight ongoing work, and help shape the future of Debezium together.

We look forward to seeing you there!
